public_rationale: The October 2025 message study found existential-risk messages comparatively weak at mobilizing respondents; it did not measure increased support for continued incumbent development through perceived exclusive expertise [e1]. The May 2023 survey report records calls for a moratorium after a safety-risk narrative [e2]. Neither directly tests whether describing AI as unknown and uncontrollable causes the claimed shift toward letting incumbent companies continue [e1, e2].
limitations: The studies use different messages and outcomes from those specified in the claim.
Neither isolates perceived exclusive expertise as the causal mechanism.
Weak mobilization and calls for restrictions do not settle the claimed effect on support for incumbent development.

our_interpretation: Read as a claim that this framing shifts audiences or policy arguments toward allowing incumbent AI companies to continue development because of their perceived exclusive expertise.
A weaker response to existential-risk messaging is not equivalent to increased support for incumbent development.
The conditional wording states a causal mechanism, not a forecast with an activation condition or deadline.
criteria.support_condition: Comparative audience research or well-documented policy-process evidence shows that unknowability and uncontrollability framing causes greater support for continued incumbent development through perceived exclusive expertise.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Research testing that framing and outcome finds no shift, an opposite shift, or evidence inconsistent with the asserted expertise mechanism.
